about: Patches that put the shore back where it was before each harbour work (DATA.md, “Patches, on any pack”): raise patches lay dredged ground back at the reef, bar or shore it was cut from, lower patches lay fill back at the reef it was made on. Each applies to years before its `until`. A raise mask’s weights carry the reef’s relief: under the app’s mix h + (depth − h)·w, each texel goes to the reef that rims the cut, which is never shallower than `depth`. Natural passages are in passages.geojson and no raise touches them

passages.note: the passages kept open (Polygons) and, under `bars`, the bars held at their surveyed depth; lon/lat

patches.name: the cut through the Honolulu bar
patches.note: the entrance channel where it crosses the bar and the reef edge: “In 1890-92, a channel 200-feet wide by 30-feet deep was dredged for about 1,000-feet through the sand bar”, which had held ships to as little as 18 feet. Laid back at 5.5 m, the bar’s depth, where the reef beside it is shallower, and at the sea floor beside it past the reef edge; today’s cut is wider than the first

patches.name: the Pearl Harbor entrance channel and bar
patches.note: the entrance channel cut through the reef flat and the bar outside the natural channel: begun in 1902 under the 1901 appropriation, deep enough for the gunboat Petrel in January 1905, enlarged under the Act of 13 May 1908, and “completed ... December 14, 1911”, when the cruiser California entered. The 1881 channel inside the bar stays open; elsewhere the cut goes back to the reef flat or sea floor that rims it, and across the bar never shallower than 3.5 m, the bar’s depth by the surveys (the sea floor beside the bar is 6 to 8 m deep today, and the cut there goes back to that). Its later widenings are not separated
